Let’s talk about something we all face on the road to change: setbacks.
Chapter 9—Overcoming Setbacks and Building Lasting Habits.
You know, change hardly ever moves in a straight line. There’ll be days when old habits just sneak back in. Maybe stress, or even a celebration, leads you to choices that spike your glucose. Or, you might feel like your progress is crawling along.
But here’s the thing—these moments aren’t failures. They’re actually chances to practice resilience and show yourself a little compassion.
The truth is, real change is built on small, steady actions. Instead of chasing perfection, try focusing on getting back to your supportive habits after a slip. Every single meal is a fresh opportunity to nourish your body and reset.
So, what makes a habit stick? Here are a few gentle reminders that can really help:
Start small. Pick just one or two changes to focus on—like tossing some extra veggies into your lunch, or taking a stroll after dinner. Tiny shifts add up in powerful ways.
Celebrate progress. Notice those little victories. Maybe you have steadier energy, or you’re not craving sugar as much. Give yourself credit for those wins.
Anticipate challenges. Life gets busy, right? So, plan ahead for those days—maybe pack a healthy snack or scout out supportive food options before you head out.
Seek support. Share your goals with friends, family, or even a group that gets what you’re working toward. Encouragement and accountability can make all the difference.
Think of habits like trails winding through a forest. The more you walk them, the clearer and easier they become. After a while, those routines just feel natural—and keeping them up takes way less effort.
It’s also worth reframing setbacks as learning moments. Say you travel for a week, eat more sugar, and move less. Instead of beating yourself up, check in with your body—how do you feel? Use that info to help guide your choices next time.
This journey is ongoing, and every experience teaches you something new.
When you bring patience and self-kindness to the process, building habits that support your glucose and overall well-being really does become possible—for the long haul.
